Does the Unabomber wish to Destroy Us All?

Subject: Does the Unabomber wish to Destroy Us All?
Message-ID: <32CD5EE8.7B36@erols.com>

Matched passages: §167 · §168 · §169 · §170

Download original message (.eml)

Several people have expressed the idea that the Unabomber wished to rule the 
world, deprive others of their freedom, or "destroy us all". (meaning, wipe out 
humanity?)

They probably came to this conclusion because they know that "getting rid of 
technology" would cause a lot of suffering. Now I'll admit that the Unabomber's 
proposed revolution would be a very drastic step, but I don't believe he 
advocates wholesale slaughter. I looked in the Manifesto and found this section 
on the topic.

HUMAN SUFFERING
167. ... if the breakdown is sudden, many people will die, since the world 
population has become so overblown that it cannot even feed itself.. without 
advanced technology.... is it therefore cruel to work for the breakdown of the 
system? Maybe, but maybe not. ...revolutionaries will not be able to break the 
system down unless it is already in deep trouble, so that there would be a good 
chance of its eventually breaking down by itself anyway; and the bigger the 
system grows, the more disastrous the consequences of its breakdown will be; so 
it may be that revolutionaries, by hastening the onset of the breakdown, will be 
reducing the extent of the disaster."

 168. ...one has to balance the struggle and death against the loss of freedom & 
dignity... [kind of like the Cold War military leaders who thought mass death 
from  nuclear war was preferable to being conquered by the Reds.]

169. ...it is not at all certain that the survival of the system will lead to 
less suffering than the breakdown of the system would. The system has already 
caused, and is continuing to cause, immense suffering all over the world... [he 
describes the disruptions of ancient cultures & ecosystems in the 3rd world and 
the psych. disruptions in the West, and goes on with this sentence: "would you 
like to speculate about what Iraq or North Korea will do with genetic 
engineering?"]

170....ending sentence. "technology has gotten the human race into a fix from 
which there is not likely to be any easy escape."

end of Manifesto quote.

What he seems to be saying is that technology is to humans what heroin is to 
junkies. Withdrawal is very painful, but not to withdraw would eventually lead 
to death. 

--Shadow
